title: Note On Fair Copy And Correspondence

questions.question: Why does the note say some ideas from other books were written again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because those other parts were not there, so some important points were included again.

questions.question: What did they want the students in that area to write?
questions.answer: A small complete copy of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Even though there seemed to be repetition, what did they still have the students write down?
questions.answer: The whole treatise that was there.

questions.question: Who wrote the corrected copy of the rough draft?
questions.answer: A blessed person.

questions.question: What was surprising about that person?
questions.answer: He did not know much about those matters, but something special still appeared in his copy.

questions.question: What special pattern was seen in the copy?
questions.answer: The letters at the starts of the lines matched in a meaningful way.

questions.question: How many alifs were counted at the beginnings of the lines?
questions.answer: Six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: What is an alif?
questions.answer: The first letter of the Arabic alphabet.

questions.question: What title matched that number in abjad value?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: Whose naming of the treatise is mentioned?
questions.answer: Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

questions.question: What did this number match show about the title?
questions.answer: It showed the title fit the treatise well.

questions.question: What else did the writers understand from this number match?
questions.answer: They saw it as a sign that the treatise came as a light from Qur’an verses.

questions.question: Where were the other parts of the Risale-i Nur missing from?
questions.answer: From the place where this treatise was written.

questions.question: Which two works are named as having important matters mentioned again?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: Is the repeated writing described as hidden or easy to notice?
questions.answer: It is described as something easy to notice.

questions.question: Why did they still want the present treatise written down fully?
questions.answer: So the students there could make a small but complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What kind of copy was later revised?
questions.answer: A rough first draft.

questions.question: How is the person who wrote the revised copy described?
questions.answer: As a blessed person.

questions.question: Did that person know a lot about these special matters?
questions.answer: No, he was unaware of them.

questions.question: What was noticed in his writing?
questions.answer: A fine and deep matching in the letters.

questions.question: Where were the counted alifs found?
questions.answer: At the beginning of the lines.

questions.question: What does the note say the number 666 matched?
questions.answer: The abjad value of the treatise’s title.

questions.question: How did they connect this to the Qur’an too?
questions.answer: They said it also pointed to the treatise being a light taken from Qur’an verses, which they gave as 6,666 in number.

questions.question: What problem came from the other parts not being available?
questions.answer: Some important teachings had to be repeated in this treatise.

questions.question: What does the note say about this repetition?
questions.answer: It may look like repetition.

questions.question: What good purpose did that repetition serve for the local students?
questions.answer: It helped them write a small complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What happened to the first draft after it was written?
questions.answer: A revised copy of it was made.

questions.question: What kind of person made that revised copy?
questions.answer: A blessed person.

questions.question: Why is it interesting that this person made the special pattern?
questions.answer: Because he did not know about such things.

questions.question: What letter was counted again and again in the copy?
questions.answer: Alif.

questions.question: How many of those letters were counted at line beginnings?
What title had the same number value?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What conclusion was drawn from the matching numbers?
questions.answer: That the title was suitable for the treatise.

questions.question: What bigger meaning did they also take from this sign?
questions.answer: That the treatise was connected to the light of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What was not on hand when the treatise was being composed?
questions.answer: The other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Because of that, what happened in The Supreme Sign?
questions.answer: Important points from other books were mentioned there too.

questions.question: What are the names of those other books?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: What job were the students in that area given?
questions.answer: Writing down the whole treatise.

questions.question: What was the reason for giving them that job?
questions.answer: To help them produce a miniature complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What kind of draft is mentioned before the revised copy?
questions.answer: A rough draft.

questions.question: What was found in the revised copy?
questions.answer: A delicate and deep letter pattern.

questions.question: What made that finding more amazing?
questions.answer: The person who wrote it was not learned in those matters.

questions.question: Which letter is explained in a footnote?
questions.answer: Alif.

questions.question: What two facts are given about alif in the footnote?
questions.answer: It is the first Arabic letter, and its number value is one.

questions.question: What number of alifs was counted?
What two things did that number point to?
questions.answer: The fitting title Ayat al-Kubra and a sign of connection to the Qur’an’s verses.

questions.question: In simple words, why were some ideas repeated in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because the other books were missing there.

questions.question: What does the note call that repetition?
questions.answer: Something that appears to be repetition.

questions.question: What did they hope the students would end up with by writing it all?
questions.answer: A small but complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Was only part of the treatise written down, or all of it?
questions.answer: All of it.

questions.question: Who prepared the revised copy?
questions.answer: A blessed person.

questions.question: Did he make the pattern on purpose because he knew the subject well?
questions.answer: No, he did not know such matters.

questions.question: What careful detail was noticed in the copy?
questions.answer: The first letters of the lines showed a meaningful count.

questions.question: What was that count?
questions.answer: 666 alifs.

questions.question: What title is said to have the same abjad number?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, meaning The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: Who is said to have given that title?
questions.answer: Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

questions.question: What did the matching number show about the title and the book?
questions.answer: It showed the title suited the book.

questions.question: What did they believe the match hinted about the source of the treatise’s light?
questions.answer: That it was a shining reflection from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the main reason given for mentioning some earlier topics again?
questions.answer: The needed books were not available where this one was written.

questions.question: What is the name of the treatise being talked about in the note?
questions.answer: The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What was the goal for the students in that region?
questions.answer: To write a miniature full Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What was revised after the first writing?
questions.answer: The rough draft.

questions.question: How is the person who wrote the revised version described in a good way?
questions.answer: As blessed.

questions.question: What did the writers notice in his copy?
questions.answer: A subtle and deep matching of letters.

questions.question: At what place in the lines were the alifs counted?
questions.answer: At the starts of the lines.

questions.question: What number was reached?
What does the note say that number fully agrees with?
questions.answer: The abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What idea about the title came from that agreement?
questions.answer: That the title was very suitable.

questions.question: What second sign did they understand from the same number?
questions.answer: That the treatise was a flash from the light of Qur’an verses.

questions.question: Why does the Qur’an also connect with the number 666 in the note?
questions.answer: Because the note says the Qur’an’s verses are 6,666 in number.
